reviews.notes:
I built r5_design.html and wrapped it with the viewport meta as /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-photoStamper/bb344c8a-11d1-57c4-b6a1-fd224fa30cfd/scratchpad/qa/r5_design_wrapped.html. Screenshots are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-photoStamper/bb344c8a-11d1-57c4-b6a1-fd224fa30cfd/scratchpad/qa/r5_design/: one per section and context, viewport sequences in vp/, and reader captures in xr/. Scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-photoStamper/bb344c8a-11d1-57c4-b6a1-fd224fa30cfd/scratchpad/qa/r5_design_scripts/.

**Round-4 design fixes I confirmed in the render:**
- #xmFig: inline key, chevrons, 'Now only' default on phone, fade and swipe cue.
- #xrLang: legend line, and disabled languages at 40% opacity with no hatch.
- #xrHd: line two names the glossed word for Hebrew.
- Column rules are neutral.
- #oct7: the empty ', )' romanization slot is gone.
- #organised: the bloc-card layout is no longer relevant.

**Still open from round 4 deferrals:**
- Arabic 'captive' and Polish 'label' glyphs (issue 7).
- Morph not capped at 600ms (issue 8c).

**New since the EIC cut:**
- The layers legend was removed, so the CONTENT/PROCESS/SOURCES tags are now orphaned (issue 9).
- #charge and #against lost their charts (issue 10).
- The scrolly uses red for every battle, which conflicts with the council rule that red dashed means 7 Oct only (issue 1).

**Minor items not ranked:**
- On phone, the pinned #zionism stepper turns 'stuck' while the chips and the 'How to read this' text are still on screen, and briefly covers them.
- At 1280 the #zionism figure has about 120px of empty space under the BEFORE/AFTER panels.
- The desktop page shows 'WIKIPEDIA FRAMING DRIFT' twice, at the right of the tab bar and again in the masthead.
- In dark mode, the pale 'written in that week' bars in the scrolly sit close to the background (dark teal on near-black).

**Language-barrier visuals score (6.5):** the story-layer grid is strong and faithful. The reader in the Evidence room is good once it settles. The gap is that the story itself shows no original words, and the bridge to the reader is a one-way tab switch.

strengths: The EIC cut made the story view much cleaner: 16,402px on phone and 13,334px at 1280. None of the 8 contexts (story and evidence, phone and desktop, light and dark) has page-level horizontal overflow (scrollWidth equals the viewport), and none has a script error; the only failure is the blocked web-font request. Every story section keeps the house scaffolding: eyebrow, finding-led H2, ruled 'Bottom line', a figure card with 'How to read this', and a mono legend.

Several round-4 UI fixes really landed. The #ziCtl stepper has a compact stuck state (66px instead of 140px), docks at the foot of the figure, and no longer leaves the blank placeholder. #ppSide ('Israel | Hamas | Other') and #xrTime ('Then · 2024 | Now · 2026 | Both') sit on one row. Every phone .seg button in both views measures 40–42px. #ziMoments, #o7Moments, #xrArts and #xmScroll have the fade mask, and the matrix has its 'swipe for 4 more claims →' cap.

The #organised Groups view now uses the stacked bloc rows asked for in rounds 1–4. Each window label is a full-width line, followed by its stat line and a full-width dumbbell. The #xwGG genocide-article figure now uses native names with codes, a 0/500/1000-day axis, ticks and 'none' rows, matching the matrix. The story copy of the network has a bottom-sticky detail panel ('Tap or tab to an account…') that stays in view while the reader explores the graph.

Dark mode is fully themed across the new material: the scrolly's teal bars and red battle rules, inverted .seg selected states, matrix glyphs, network nodes and rings, and the evidence-room charts. The scope box and the trust can/can't box read well in both themes.

Components are reused, not invented. One Prev/Play/Next stepper serves #zionism, #o7Fig and #xrFig. The '+ LABEL caption' disclosure is used for FULL KEY, OUR CODING and MORE. Quote cards share the swatch-plus-mono-header card. The diff chips under the Zionism H2 use the amber-struck and blue-added grammar of the rest of the page.

DESK VERDICT: We would run this as a weekend longread plus a 3-minute evening segment ('What the world now reads about us'), not as breaking news. That holds only once the ArbCom line (issue 1) is verified or cut and the uneven treatment of recent edits (issue 2) is fixed.

ON-AIR 60 SECONDS: run four visuals in this order, all already on the page:
- the Zionism word chips;
- the Israel genocide quote card with the denial line;
- the Hamas designation-position chart;
- the Nakba 2021/2026 card.
The October 7 then/now strip from issue 3 is the missing fifth.

PROPOSED HEADLINE: Wikipedia now says Israel “began committing genocide”, that Zionism came “through colonization”, and that October 7 was “armed incursions”

DEK: A revision-by-revision study of English Wikipedia, 2021–2026. The opening lines on Zionism, 1948, October 7 and Hamas were rewritten, many first in the weeks after the war's major battles, and the hostages have never been in October 7's first sentence.

P1: English Wikipedia's article on Israel, viewed 4.6 million times in the past 12 months, now says in the encyclopedia's own voice: “After the Hamas-led October 7 attacks, Israel began committing genocide against Palestinians in Gaza.” The next sentence is Israel's denial. Among the 150 most-read opening sections that existed in 2021, none charged Israel with genocide in January 2021 or July 2023; seven do now, two in Wikipedia's own voice.

P2: The answer to “what is Zionism?” changed too. In January 2021 its first sentence spoke of “the re-establishment of and support for a Jewish state in the territory defined as the historic Land of Israel”. Today Zionism is a movement for “a Jewish homeland through colonization”, a wording that has stood since 27 August 2026. The Nakba is now “the ethnic cleansing of Palestinian Arabs by Zionists”. The 1948 Palestine war article still says “Hundreds of thousands of Jews fled or were expelled from Arab states”, naming no one.

P3: The first sentence of the October 7 article calls the attack “a series of coordinated armed incursions”. Across 107 versions of that sentence, “massacre” stood for about an hour in total, and the hostages never appeared; they are in sentence 9. Five days after the attack Hamas lost “militant” from its definition; it is now “a political organisation with a military wing”, and the sentence on its terror designation moved from sentence 5 to 22 of 23. Some edits went the other way, far fewer: 61 critical terms out against 223 in. The timing follows the battles, but it does not prove why anyone edited. Our tests found no sign of a large organised campaign, and no editor is named.

NARRATIVE-LED CHECK:
- H2s lead with the narrative in #zionism, #after, #charge, #oct7, #palestine and #crosslang.
